correctness.rationale: For a strictly positive periodic solution, period integration converts the delayed top-predator birth term into a contemporaneous period integral by shift invariance. Normalizing by the positive top-predator mass yields an exact weighted identity. Strict denominator comparison and Jensen's inequality for the concave map \(u/(v+pu)\) give the threshold and force \(\eta>pe\). When \(\tau_2=0\), averaging \(d(\log x_3)/dt\) yields the ordinary-mean version. The proof explicitly withholds that logarithmic step for positive \(\tau_2\). The packaged exact-arithmetic checker verifies the threshold algebra but is not the proof.

value.rationale: The source studies delay-driven Hopf oscillations, but its threshold \(ve/(\eta-pe)\) is presented only through equilibrium positivity and local invasion. The new theorem carries that same threshold to every finite-amplitude positive periodic state, for arbitrary delays in a natural top-predator-weighted mean and for the ordinary time mean on the \(\tau_2=0\) Hopf slice. This supplies a nonlocal consistency check and a structural ecological interpretation that is not a routine parameter substitution or a numerical recomputation.
